title: Thousands of Giant Spider Crabs Pile Up in One Australian Bay

scenes.text: Thousands of crabs gather in one bay.
It happens every year in Port Phillip Bay, near Melbourne.
They gather before the winter moult, when they shed their shells.
Moulting takes up to an hour, and the new shell is soft.
Soft crabs are easy prey for rays, seals and birds.
So they pile up in huge numbers, and safety is in the crowd.

description:
Thousands of giant spider crabs gather every year in Port Phillip Bay near Melbourne, the largest known gathering of the species.
The leading theory is that they group up for safety while their new shells harden after moulting.
Would you dive in to see it?
first_comment: Would you dive in with thousands of crabs?
